chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That a man from the Muslims converted to Christianity, and he was brought before the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). He invited him to repent (to return to Islam), but he refused. He grabbed his hair, then said: 'Tread on the slaves of Allah,' so he was trodden upon until he died.

key_terms.اسْتَتَابَهُ: He invited him to repent/return to Islam

ai.seo_question: What happened to the apostate man when he was brought before Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* illustrates the early juristic view of apostasy (*murtad*) as a capital offense, specifically highlighting the method of execution by trampling (*taw'*) which distinguishes it from the sword. It reflects the historical context of Imam Ali’s governance where public renunciation of Islam was treated as a political and religious breach, leading to the companion's death after refusing repentance. This narrative is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the severity of leaving the fold of Islam in the early community.
